summary: Date field with typeable segments and a calendar in a popover; supports dates without time, dates with time, and zoned instants.
whenToUse: Dates in forms, with fast typing and an optional calendar.
whenNotToUse: Date and time with a time list: use DateTimePicker.
Time only: use TimePicker or TimeInput.

props.name: value / defaultValue / onChange
props.description: The value type determines the meaning: civil date or zoned instant.

props.name: firstDayOfWeek
props.description: First day of the week in the calendar.

props.name: presets
props.description: Shortcuts in the popover. "default": Today/Tomorrow/In a week (range: Last 7/30 days, This month, Last month). Out-of-range shortcuts are disabled.

props.name: showMonthYearPicker
props.description: Month and year selectors in the calendar header.

props.name: calendarErrorMessage
props.description: Message in the calendar for unavailable dates.

props.name: name (startName / endName)
props.description: ISO values submitted with the form.

inherits: react-aria-components DatePicker / DateRangePicker props (hourCycle, hideTimeZone, validate…).

keyboard.action: Next segment, then the calendar button.
Opens the calendar; Esc closes it and focus returns to the field.

accessibility: Segments as labeled spinbuttons; button with the localized name “Open calendar”.
The popover is a dialog with focus on the selected date and focus restored on close.
The popover inherits the theme of the originating ThemeProvider, even when nested.
responsive: The field shrinks with the container; the popover stays within the viewport and months wrap.
customization: className on the field, popoverProps.className on the popover.
commonMistakes: Converting a CalendarDate to a JavaScript Date with toDate(local time zone) and then serializing to UTC: the day can shift. Serialize with toString().
Using ZonedDateTime for civil dates (birthdays, deadlines): use CalendarDate.
Expecting onChange on every keystroke: the value is committed when the field is complete and loses focus.
limits: With ZonedDateTime, changing the day across a daylight saving time transition can shift the local time (e.g. 01:30 → 02:30): this is @internationalized/date behavior and should be verified in critical cases.
